anomalies.observed: On the CAN BUS sheet, the second isolated CAN transceiver U10 (driven by MCP2515 U9) outputs its bus lines to nets labelled 'CAN_L_P' (pin 7) and 'CAN_L_N' (pin 6) — note the letter 'L'. The two M12 CAN connectors J2 ('CAN Interface A') and J3 ('CAN Interface B') instead bring out pins 2/3 as 'CAN1_P'/'CAN1_N' (digit '1'). Because the net names differ, U10's CAN bus never reaches either connector, and the connectors' CAN1_P/CAN1_N pins are undriven (and also miss the D9/D10 TVS protection, which the spec places on CAN1_P/N).
anomalies.expected: Per the spec, the board implements 'two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 ... broken out on M12 circular connectors', with TVS arrays D9/D10 on 'CAN0_P/N, CAN1_P/N'. The CAN1 transceiver's output nets must share the same name as the connector pins (CAN1_P/CAN1_N) so that U9/U10 actually drive the second CAN bus out to the connectors.

anomalies.impact: The second CAN bus (CAN1, from U9/U10) is electrically disconnected from the external M12 connectors: the connectors' CAN1 pins float and the transceiver's CAN_L lines go nowhere, so any Odrive/actuator on the CAN1 bus cannot communicate, and that bus also loses its SM712 transient protection.
